intent: Submit a Questionnaire from its last item, after every enabled item passes validation.
typical_uses: The final action of a questionnaire's navigation row

dont_use_when.situation: An action button outside a questionnaire

invariants.text: `variant` and `size` are passed to the kit Button the component renders by default; when `render` is given it replaces that Button and both are ignored.

It is visible only on the last item, sharing the cell QuestionnaireNext leaves there. While hidden it carries the native `hidden` and `inert` attributes, `aria-hidden` and tabIndex -1, and `data-hidden` in place of `data-visible`.
It renders a `type="submit"` button, so activating it submits the form and the root's validation of every item runs before `onSubmit`.

anti_patterns.dont: Submit the answers from a click handler on QuestionnaireSubmit
anti_patterns.do_instead: Handle the root's `onSubmit`; it is called only after every item passes, with the form's data ready to read

a11y.by: questionnaire.test.tsx asserts Submit has the hidden property before the last item and loses it there

render.states: render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies
render.because: The questionnaire engine's render prop takes an element or a function of the button's own state (`QuestionnaireNavigationState`: disabled, shortcut, status, visible), so its type is a union of a React element and a callback; the compiler emits one JSON type per property, so nothing is asserted. The kit defaults it to its own Button.

good.title: A smaller Submit button with its own text

bad.title: Submission handled on the button
bad.why: The click runs before the root validates, so it saves answers the questionnaire is about to reject; the root's `onSubmit` is the one called only once every item passes.

render.description: TS: RenderProp<QuestionnaireNavigationState> | undefined. The compiler emits one JSON type per property; this type is left to tsc. render replaces the rendered element with one the caller supplies.
